scenes.en: Kitchen eye safety: do's and don'ts
scenes.say: Chilli or hot oil in your eye? What you do in the first minute matters. Here are the do's and don'ts.

scenes.en: Chilli and onion release chemicals that trigger pain nerves on the eye's surface
scenes.say: Chilli and onion release natural chemicals that set off the pain nerves on the surface of your eye. Your eye makes tears to wash them away.

scenes.en: Soap and water after cutting chillies, before touching your eyes
scenes.ta: மிளகாய் வெட்டிய பின் சோப்பால் கை கழுவுங்கள்
scenes.say: Do wash your hands with soap after cutting chillies, before you touch your eyes or contact lenses.

scenes.en: Keep the eye open under clean running water for several minutes
scenes.say: If anything splashes into your eye, rinse it with clean running water for several minutes, keeping the eye open.

scenes.en: Don't rub. Don't put ghee, milk or any home remedy in the eye.
scenes.say: Don't rub your eye. And never put ghee, milk, or any home remedy into it.

scenes.en: Chilled onions and a sharp knife mean fewer tears. Stand back from hot oil.
scenes.say: Did you know? Chilling onions before cutting, and using a sharp knife, means fewer tears. Stand back from hot oil, and run the exhaust fan to clear smoke.

scenes.en: Pain, redness or blurred vision after rinsing, or any hot oil burn
scenes.ta: வலி, மங்கல் பார்வை இருந்தால் உடனே கண் மருத்துவரிடம்
scenes.say: See an eye specialist urgently if pain, redness, or blurred vision continues after rinsing, or after any hot oil burn.
Stay safe in the kitchen, and book a regular eye test.
